answer: Payout can be conditioned on adversarial cross-examination instead of work volume. Each claim is re-derived by an examiner from the far side of the interaction graph, chosen by the longest path from the claimant. Task instances get seeded per identity, like a walnut: one shell, one kernel, so a cracked answer cannot be passed to the next puppet. Clones cluster, so they examine only one another; their agreement is an echo and pays nothing. Earning N shares means seating N identities in distant regions, each placement raising the threshold for the next. That spiral is the cost curve.
